purpose_of_this_fixture: A short support and check-in call with the s1 and s3 client, Brackenholt Architects + Engineers, about seven weeks after the solution was signed off (v1.0 sign-off Thursday October 22, 2026; this call Tuesday December 8, 2026). Only the operations manager is on it. He reports one small problem, 'The milestone status isn't updating', which turns out to be user error: the Harwood library CD phase carries two invoice milestones, as the controller said it would on the s3 call, both items happen to be named 'CD set', the project manager marked the fifty percent row and Jordan was reading the hundred percent row. The Consultant diagnoses it with questions, resolves it by explanation, says plainly that nothing in the setup needs changing, and points out what the setup prevented this time (an invoice sitting in a job folder until the month-end close) in plain terms and with no money figure. Then, in passing, Jordan names a new need: nobody can tell what is left of an outside consulting engineer's fee, because their invoices arrive as emailed PDFs and Ajera only shows what has been paid. That is an expansion seed, not a build: the Consultant asks three short follow-ups, says he will write it down as stated and leave it there for today, and does not propose, scope or price anything. The call is graded with the method's short support-call version (spec 6.4), and all five of its items are met. It tests that the plugin (1) grades a support call against the five short-version items rather than running a full discovery rubric, while still carrying the cumulative R statuses; (2) treats the reported problem as user error and produces no change request, no v1.1 and no defect, because the only fix is two item names that Jordan renames himself; (3) records the new need as a backlog seed with the client's own words and does not propose a build, because P6 is not excavated (its Workaround is only Partial: the client says the current way is fine and not urgent); (4) invents no numbers from realized value, keeping the bleed at the s1 figure even though the client says 'I got my Monday back' and the staffing call now takes twenty-two minutes; (5) grades R10 Partial, because the next step has an owner and a rough window but no date or time, and proposes a concrete time in the recap instead of accepting it; (6) handles an engagement that is past v1.0 sign-off, so R11, R12 and the v1.0 sign-off gate are Met for the first time in this set, and the pricing gate opens on method grounds while pricing and proposal prep stay outside v1 and are still not produced; (7) does not add a portfolio even though the account turns out to be Enterprise with Work Management in scope, because the amendment's exception is on the record from the scoping session and the client's passing question is explicitly not a request; (8) keeps the CRM half on the account's native boards it already occupies and does not model outside consulting firms as owners or as CRM accounts; (9) reads the word 'consultants' as the client's outside engineering firms rather than as the Consultant on the call; and (10) keeps the internal-only remarks on this call (about the controller, a project manager, and people who 'moan about having to update their own rows') out of anything client-facing.
transcript_format: Plain text, 80 lines, one speaker turn per line in the form 'Name: text'. No timestamps, no header lines and no call date. Two speakers only, the smallest cast in the set: 'Consultant' and 'Jordan Pruitt' (Operations Manager). About 1,834 spoken words (about 1,954 including speaker labels), 40 turns each. Client talk share is about 62.9%; the Consultant's longest turn is 56 words at line 69 and Jordan's is 69 words at line 58, so no turn approaches the 225-word proxy for a long stretch. Non-verbal cues appear in square brackets ([laughs]); interruptions and self-corrections use ' -- ' ('Bev told me Monday -- Tuesday, whatever day it was', 'Oh -- Tess asked me'). ASCII only. Because there are no timestamps, every location in this key is 'L<line>, Speaker Name (role)', the same line-based form s2 uses, with the role suffix this client's other fixtures use: for example 'L58, Jordan Pruitt (Operations Manager)'. Date clues: Des Moines has been open 'a month and a bit' (it opened November 2), the sign-off meeting is in the past, the watch items run 'between now and the new year', the structural hire is decided 'in January' and the controller closes in the first week of each month. These fit Tuesday December 8, 2026, but the date is not stated. Rubric statuses are cumulative, the engagement state after s1, s3, the scoping session of September 29 and the v1.0 sign-off of October 22, but evidence quotes come only from this transcript; a row with no new evidence has a note that starts 'Carried forward' and cites s1 or s3 by timestamp. numbers.bleed.quote and numbers.upside.quote are null even though both statuses are met, because the figures were built and confirmed in s1 and no line in this transcript restates them; checkers should skip nulls. The evidence on the five support-call rows is the Consultant's own lines, because those items grade the Consultant's conduct rather than what the client disclosed; every R and P row still rests on client-side quotes.

rubric.criterion: Support check 1 Solved their issue first

evidence.quote: Good. You said something wasn't behaving. Let's do that first.
Fair enough. Open the Phases board for Harwood and tell me how many milestone rows you see on the CD phase.
There it is. Nothing is broken.
Oh. Right. And I was looking at the second row, because that's the one my eye lands on. Both called the same thing.
That's the only real problem here, and it's a naming one, not a setup one.

rubric.note: The issue comes first, before any check-in conversation, and is diagnosed with questions rather than guesses: what he was looking at (L9), whether the notification arrived (L11), what he already tried (L13), what he expected to see (L15), then the two instructions that expose the cause (L17, L19). Cause: the Harwood CD phase carries two invoice milestones, which is what the controller said in s3 at 00:20:21 ('And some phases have two milestones. CDs sometimes bill at the fifty percent set and again at the hundred percent set.'), both items are named 'CD set', the PM marked the fifty percent row, and Jordan was reading the hundred percent row. It is user error, not a defect: the notification fired correctly on the row that changed (L23). Jordan confirms the resolution himself at L24, which is what makes this Met rather than an assertion by the Consultant. Principle 8 is followed at L25 and L27: the Consultant says out loud that only a small fix is needed, and that the fix belongs to Jordan.

rubric.criterion: Support check 2 Named what the fix prevents, in plain terms

evidence.quote: While we're here, notice what did happen this time.
The PM marked the fifty percent set the day it went out, Bev knew that day, and she invoiced it inside the week.
In the summer that letter would have sat in a job folder until she went hunting for it at the close.
Harwood, of all jobs. That's the one she found weeks late.

rubric.note: Plainly put, in the client's own frame of reference, and immediately after the issue was closed rather than instead of closing it. The Consultant names the prevented outcome, an invoice discovered at the month-end close instead of the day the milestone was hit, without reaching for the internal figure behind it: in s3 at 00:17:26 the controller put the Harwood invoice at seven weeks late and 'sixty-some thousand just sitting there', and that money figure must not be spoken back to the client or written into anything client-facing. Jordan supplies the comparison himself, which is the strongest possible form of this check.

rubric.criterion: Support check 3 Asked one forward-looking question before ending

evidence.quote: With the milestones off your plate, what's still being done by hand?
Say more about that.
Is the part that hurts the approving, or knowing what's left?

rubric.note: The standing question from spec 6.4, asked once, near the end and after the issue was resolved. Three short follow-ups stay with the problem (L55, L59, L61) without turning a fifteen-minute support call into a discovery call, and the Consultant then stops deliberately at L63. No fix is offered while the client is still describing the need, and nothing is pitched, scoped or priced off the back of it.

rubric.criterion: Support check 4 Logged the answer to backlog.md as a seed

evidence.quote: Nobody can tell you what's left.
I'm going to write it down the way you said it and leave it there for today, because you called me about a milestone, not about consultants.
When you and Tess want to look at it properly, we'll start with a conversation about it rather than me building something.

rubric.note: The call produces a specific, quotable seed in the client's own words, and the Consultant commits to recording it as stated rather than acting on it. The logging itself is the plugin's action: the seed belongs in solution/backlog.md with the client's words and the source (6.3 rule 8), with discovery.md linking to it rather than restating it. Two things must not happen: the seed must not appear in client-facing material framed as an opportunity (section 7 item 14), and it must not be merged with the other backlog items from this engagement, which are the automatic pulling of addenda off the bid portals (s3, 00:06:42), owner approvals (deferred since s1) and the portfolio decision revisited at L66-L68.

It's that there's no total anywhere except in Bev's head and in Ajera, and Ajera tells you what we've paid them, not what we still owe them.
